note.note:
Consult Summary:
- 51-year-old female with 6 days of dysuria, malodorous urine, intermittent midline lower abdominal pain and spotting hematuria; clinician suspects urinary tract infection and prescribed a 3-day course of antibiotics to be sent to the patient's chosen pharmacy.

History:
- Presenting complaint:
  - Pain on urination (dysuria) for 6 days.
  - Unpleasant/foul smell of urine.
  - Spotting blood in urine over same 6-day period.
  - Intermittent lower abdominal (suprapubic) pain, midline, pain severity reported as 7/10, comes and goes.
- Timeline:
  - Symptoms began 6 days prior to consultation and have persisted.
  - No prior episodes of similar symptoms; patient reports never having had urinary symptoms before.
- Exacerbating/relieving factors:
  - No specific initiating events identified (no recent heavy exercise, dehydration, or increased sexual activity reported).
  - Doctor advised increased oral fluids (2.5–3 L/day) and suggested cranberry juice and over-the-counter urinary alkalinizing sachets as adjuncts.
- Associated symptoms / systems review:
  - No fever or subjective fevers reported.
  - No loin or lower back pain reported (transcript contains ambiguous phrasing regarding back pain; see conflicts).
  - No vaginal discharge reported.
  - Regular menstrual periods.
  - No change in bowel habits, no weight loss.
  - Able to pass urine, no retention reported.
- Pertinent negatives:
  - No fever, no loin/renal flank pain, no vaginal discharge, no prior UTIs per patient.

Past Medical History:
- Irritable bowel syndrome (IBS).
  - Medication: Mebeverine 200 mg, taken three times daily (patient reports regular use).
- No other medical problems or prior surgeries reported.
- Allergies:
  - Clindamycin (allergy reported).

Social History:
- Living situation: lives with friends.
- Occupation: support worker.
- Alcohol: occasional; reports approximately one glass of wine per week.
- Smoking: denies tobacco use.
- No recreational drug use documented.

Family History:
- Patient reports no family medical problems.

Physical Examination:
- No vital signs documented.
- No physical examination findings documented.

Investigations:
- No investigations performed during this consult.
- Clinician recommended patient obtain a thermometer and check temperature at home.
- No urinary dipstick, microscopy, culture, pregnancy test, or imaging documented.

Assessment & Plan:
- Issue 1: Suspected lower urinary tract infection (acute cystitis)
  - Assessment: Clinical impression consistent with urinary tract infection given dysuria, malodorous urine, hematuria, and suprapubic pain.
  - Plan:
    - Antibiotic prescribed for a 3-day course; prescription to be sent to the patient's selected pharmacy (Knightsbridge Practice pharmacy). — antibiotic name/dose/route/frequency not documented.
    - Start antibiotics as soon as medications are picked up.
    - Advise increased oral fluids (recommended 2.5–3 liters/day).
    - Recommend adjuncts: cranberry juice and over-the-counter urinary alkalinizing sachets (patient advised these may help; clinician will document details in notes).
    - Obtain and monitor temperature at home; clinician advised to check for fever.
    - Return/seek urgent care if symptoms worsen, do not settle, develop high temperature, develop new lower back/loin pain, or have difficulty passing urine.
    - No routine follow-up required if symptoms resolve; return for reassessment if symptoms recur.
- Issue 2: Irritable bowel syndrome (stable)
  - Assessment: History of IBS; no current change in bowel habit or symptoms reported.
  - Plan:
    - Continue Mebeverine 200 mg three times daily as currently taken.
- Issue 3: Drug allergy — Clindamycin
  - Assessment: Allergy to clindamycin reported.
  - Plan:
    - Document allergy and avoid prescribing clindamycin.

General plan items:
- Prescription will be sent to Knightsbridge Practice pharmacy; patient advised to allow approximately one hour for processing and to collect at earliest convenience.
- Clinician to add details regarding non-prescription urinary sachets/adjuncts to the medical record.

Quality checks (document_quality):
- Missing but clinically expected elements:
  - No vital signs documented (temperature, heart rate, blood pressure).
  - No urine testing documented (dipstick, microscopy, culture) despite hematuria being present.
  - No pregnancy status or pregnancy test documented (appropriate in reproductive-age females with urinary symptoms/hematuria).
  - Antibiotic name, dose, route, and frequency not documented in transcript.
  - No physical examination findings documented.
- Internal conflicts from transcript:
  - Minor ambiguity regarding lower back pain: patient initially stated no lower back pain, then there is an unclear phrase (“No, I've got.”) followed by “and no loin pain as well.” Conflict noted about the phrasing; overall report interpreted as no flank/loin pain.
- Transcript quality:
  - Overall clear and audible with some brief clarifications and minor conversational repetitions; adequate for clinical documentation.
